summary: Iteration 6: checked the Yjs canvas sync fix and Clip Studio Phase 1, both backend and frontend. CANVAS: all requested checks pass. Admin and a TEST collaborator in two browser contexts: a note added by admin showed up live for the collaborator; adds made at the same moment by both users (a note and a frame) were both kept; a move by admin showed up for the collaborator; a delete by the collaborator showed up for admin; the collaborator's zoom to 173% left admin at 100% with item positions unchanged; reloading restored the items, and each user's viewport came back from localStorage. Live typing in notes syncs. Undo/redo of moves syncs to the other user. Clicking a note body with the link tool creates an edge, and undo/redo of the edge works. The canvas context bar 'Clip' button opens /studio. CLIP STUDIO UI: Media 'Open in Clip Studio' opens /studio/<id> with Clip 1 (video 1:32, audio 0:17.79). Timeline scrub, the I/O keys with the amber range, ArrowRight and frame-back, New clip from In/Out, 9:16 (preview reframes), S split, segment reorder, rename, queue reorder/duplicate/delete, ctrl+z and ctrl+shift+z all work, and everything survives a reload. The Captions and AI Assist tabs show 'next phase' notes. The audio waveform renders, MP4 is disabled for audio, and trim handles plus undo work. EXPORT: 2 clips as MP4 to Download went queued, running, done with download links; the files are real H.264 1080x1920 MP4s. Audio MP3 export gave a 1.01s file for a 0.41 to 1.42 trim, which is correct. The Dropbox destination ends in error with a clear files.content.write message and still offers a download; no upload is attempted. Tools page lists projects. A collaborator gets 'Clip project not found'. BACKEND: new tests/test_clip_studio.py, 9 of 10 pass. It covers 403 for paths outside the world, 401 when unauthenticated, 404 for a collaborator on GET/source/jobs/PUT/DELETE/list, persistence, MP4 export plus ffprobe, download token rules (none/garbage/other user), Dropbox error with downloadable=true, 403 for a Dropbox folder outside the world, MP3 trim duration, 400 for a bad format and 422 for empty clip_ids. Full regression: 52 passed, 1 skipped. FAILURE: exported clip duration and A/V alignment are off (details below).

critical.issue: Exported duration does not match the sum of segments, and audio/video drift. Source '05 VishnuThrowsTejas.mp4' is 1 fps. Segments [1-2.5, 4-5] (2.5s) gave a 3.0s file (video 2.0s vs audio 1.5s for segment 1). Segments [13.8-18.4, 9.2-13.8] (9.2s) gave an 11.0s file: video stream starts at 0.2s, audio is 9.8s, and concat pads audio with silence. This reproduced every time on both the Dropbox URL and a local copy. Cause: each segment input is cut only with input -ss/-to. Nothing trims frames to the exact segment length and there is no setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, so the last frame's duration and the start offset leak into concat. Fix: per segment use '[i:v]...,fps=30,trim=duration=L,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS' and '[i:a]atrim=duration=L,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS', and/or add -t L on the output side. Optionally check the output duration against the expected total.

critical.endpoint: run_job (FFmpeg reading Dropbox temp link over HTTP)
critical.issue: INTERMITTENT, 1 of 7 MP4 renders: a 9.2s two-segment clip came out as 5.8s with 4.6s of audio, effectively missing one segment, yet ffmpeg exited 0 and the job showed 'done'. 6 later renders of the same clip all gave 11.0s, so I could not reproduce it. Likely cause: two concurrent HTTP reads of the same temp link where one gets truncated. Suggest '-reconnect 1 -reconnect_streamed 1 -reconnect_on_network_error 1' on HTTP inputs, or downloading the source once to a temp file, plus checking the output duration and marking the job as error on a mismatch.

minor.issue: When a job fails after rendering (Dropbox scope error), 'size' is not stored. The UI download link shows an icon with no size.

Every 'Open in Clip Studio' or canvas 'Clip' click creates a new duplicate project for the same file. I ended up with 3 '05 VishnuThrowsTejas' entries. Consider reusing the user's existing project for the same path, or offering 'open existing'.
clip_jobs rows and the backend/exports/*.mp4/mp3 files are not removed, and the exports dir is never cleaned up (14 files now), so disk use grows without limit.
'clips' is an untyped list with no Pydantic model for segments, aspect or crop. Malformed data is saved and then fails later inside the export job (KeyError, ValueError).

ui_bugs.issue: From code review, so likely rather than confirmed: onValueCommit calls onUpdate({}), which pushes ref.current.clips. After a mouse drag that value is already the changed state, so undo cannot revert a crop/volume drag. With the keyboard, each step is its own undo entry (verified: 4 ArrowLeft to 80%, undo gave 85%). Renaming a clip via onLive never creates an undo entry. Fix: snapshot clips on pointer-down/focus and push that snapshot on commit.
Audio-only clips show '16:9' in the queue subtitle.

issues: Section labels (IN / OUT, SEGMENTS, CROP ZOOM, VOLUME) are 10px text at white/45 on a near-black background, which is low contrast.
The 'Saved' indicator at the top right is 11px white/45 and easy to miss.
The description always reads '1080p H.264' even when MP3 or WAV is selected.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the segment timing in clips.build_cmd: per-segment trim/atrim to the exact length plus setpts/asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS, so the output duration equals the sum of segments and A/V stays aligned. Re-run tests/test_clip_studio.py::test_06 (expects 2.5s ± 0.3).
MEDIUM: Make the HTTP source reads robust (ffmpeg reconnect flags or a local temp download), and check the output duration so a truncated render fails instead of showing 'done'.
Store size on the error path when the file exists, so the download link shows it.
Remove clip_jobs and export files when a project is deleted, and add TTL cleanup of backend/exports.
Avoid creating a duplicate project on every 'Open in Clip Studio'.
Add Pydantic models for clips/segments in ProjectUpdate.
Fix slider/rename undo snapshots, hide the aspect label for audio clips, and make the export description depend on the selected format.
Raise the contrast of the inspector labels.
critical_code_review_comments: clips.py build_cmd: no trim/setpts per segment, which causes the duration and A/V errors above.
clips.py run_job: ffmpeg return code 0 is treated as success with no check that the output duration matches the expected total.
clips.py: RUN_LOCK is a global Semaphore(1), so every user's export is serialized. That is fine for MVP but the queue gets long with many clips.
clips.py download: the JWT goes in the query string (it ends up in logs and browser history). Consider a short-lived signed download token.
useClipProject: canUndo/canRedo come from refs and only update via the bump state. That works now, but is fragile.
collab.py: still no cleanup of lyric docs attached to deleted canvases (carried over from iteration 5).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows functional; export duration accuracy bug is backend

rca of the issue: Export duration mismatch: with input-side -ss/-to on a low-fps H.264 source, each segment's last decoded frame keeps its full duration (1s at 1 fps) and the first frame PTS is offset (0.2 to 0.8s). Without trim/setpts, concat sums the longer video length and pads audio with silence. Reproduction: create a clip with segments [1-2.5, 4-5] at 9:16 on the 1 fps source, export MP4, run ffmpeg -i on the result: Duration 3.0 instead of 2.5. Mitigation: per-segment trim=duration and setpts=PTS-STARTPTS (and the audio equivalents), plus an output duration check.
